value.rationale: The first nontrivial contact-threshold case on dense bipartite communities produces two different sustained phase mechanisms, at distinct natural shore-size cutoffs four and six. Besides a sharp all-state cutoff, the theorem gives every full labelled temporal basin by a universal 729-profile coefficient formula; this provides a general exact benchmark for finite excitable networks not answered by existing random-tree fluctuation criteria or threshold-one dense graph formulas.
